text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav-Spanish exchange in 1996 stood at over $17 million and is expected to increase by at least 50 percent this year, says commercial adviser in the Spanish embassy in Belgrade Jaime Gonzalez Tores.
- President of the Serb Independent Democratic Party (SDSS) Vojislav Stanimirovic criticised Croatian President Franjo Tudjman over the way he recruited Serbs for the Croatian parliament.
- Consumption of petrol produced in refineries of the Serbian Oil Industry NIS in Q1 this year is almost five times more than in the same period in 1996 but is still lower than in 1990.

- The Serbian government has made three key decisions to support agriculture - deferred farmers' tax payments to end November, enabled barter of raw materials in exchange for agricultural produce and introduced a programme for renewal of agricultural machinery, said President of the Serbian Cooperatives Association Viden Ranjdelovic.
- Spring sowing has been completed in Serbia. In Vojvodina province, 620,000 hectares of corn have been sown which is more than planned.

- In the first four months this year prices and interest rates have been stabilised, the difference between the official and black market exchange rate has been reduced and production has started growing, said Yugoslav National Bank Governor Ratko Banovic.
- Yugoslav bank AIK Banka from Senta received certificate on quality system in line with ISO 0991 from British Standards Institution (BSI).

- Serbia's concession law, to be examined by parliament Tuesday, will enable more rational use of the republic's natural wealth, create conditions for inflow of foreign capital and contribute to techological modernisation of infrastructure systems in the country, Serbian Deputy Construction minister Vojin Radevic said.
- New Democracy Party presented project for Serbia's and Yugoslavia's joining European integration processes.
NASA BORBA
- Montenegrin ruling Democratic Party of Socialists main board meeting Monday expected to show if the intra-party conflict will be settled or further deepened.
- Opposition Democratic Party main board said it would not take part in forthcoming elections if election conditions are not fair.
- Leader of Serbian Renewal Movement Vuk Draskovic accused his coalition partners -- the Democratic Party and the Civic Alliance of Serbia -- of trying to break up the coalition.
- Serbian authorities will not or cannot implement the agreement on normalisation of education in Kosovo signed at the end of 1996, said Vice-President of the Democratic League of Kosovo Fehmi Agani.
- Two main forms of ownership should coexist in Yugoslavia's agriculture sector - state and private ownership, says Yugoslav agriculture minister Nedeljko Sipovac.
- Yugoslavia is a crossroads for international black market cigarette trade, say paper's sources.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Serbian health workers starting a strike Monday and will only be treating emergency cases. Main reason for the strike are late wages.
- According to Montenegrin restructuring agency 90 percent of Montenegro's firms were restructured by end of 1997. Next phase is full privatisation.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Belgrade City Transport making plans to downsize 1,500 of its 9,000 workers, paper says.
DEMOKRATIJA
- I do not regret any statements I made about (Serbian President Slobodan) Milosevic, says Montenegrin Prime Minister MIlo Djukanovic.

- Montenegro will back (Slobodan) Milosevic's candidacy for president of Yugoslavia if Serbia puts it up, says Yugoslav Defence Minister and member of main board of Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro Pavle Bulatovic.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Galeb, late President Tito's vessel, is on sale again. Joseph Madol who bought it for three million dollars last year has not paid the sum yet and the purchase contract has been annulled.
- The first group of Norwegian rheumatic patients arrived in Institute Simo Milosevic in Igalo for two weeks of treatment. Altogether 450 patients from Norway will visit the institute by September 9.
- Fraction of People's Party of Montenegro of Bozidar Bojovic held its extraordinary party congress in Tivat, electing Bojovic as new president.
- TV Montenegro will hold special interviews with Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic Monday night and President Momir Bulatovic Tuesday night. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
